accepted_risks.issue: The required config/types.ts change (typed DevHarnessConfig.stack, .knowledge and orchestration.review_loop.review_security) is not checked by anything. Every fixture is cast with `as unknown as DevHarnessConfig`, every result is cast to Record<string, unknown>, and the stub returns `unknown`.

The default assertions do not match the impl step's 'filling every default'. (a) The sizing toEqual (lines 34, 42, 62, 105) uses only 5 keys, so a correct resolver that also fills the schema defaults split_on and merge_small_same_concern fails. Phase-code cannot edit tests, so this causes an RGR respawn. (b) The other defaults are never asserted: top-level merge_strategy, evidence, contract and require_flag, plus knowledge.impact_analysis. The null-config tests (lines 45, 133) check only enabled/commits, and an undefined config (allowed by the signature) is never tested.

The switch inputs are tested only with valid literal values. loadDevHarnessConfig (config/agents-md.ts parseAndValidateConfig) does not check stack or knowledge against accord-schema.json, so non-boolean or out-of-enum values reach the resolver. The dark-deploy guard can then turn the stack on, or change the security gate, when the user meant off.

Overwritten shared defaults go undetected because of test order. Every default state/sizing assertion runs before the partial-override test (line 88). After it, nothing re-resolves defaults and checks state or sizing. The input-mutation test (line 108) uses an input with no nested state or sizing object, and nothing checks that returned objects are fresh.

Knowledge defaults are not checked when a partial knowledge object is present. The drift_check test.each asserts only drift_check, and there is no `knowledge: {}` test. A resolver that returns the user object as-is passes every knowledge test.

The 'stack enabled means warn' default is tested only with an orchestration.review_loop object present. A stack-enabled config with no orchestration key is not tested. Neither is the case where knowledge.enabled alone must not change the gate.

TC-27 (e2e regression: harness suite plus runtime-smoke with defaults produce no stack or knowledge files) has no test in this task. The plan assigns it to a later task that extends packages/pi-accord/scripts/runtime-smoke.ts (plan.json:500). Task 1 adds no consumers of the flags, so no files can be produced yet.
Resolvers leave other documented schema defaults unfilled, so later tasks will re-implement them.
TC-29 also requires check:types and check:bundle on the change; unit test cannot prove them, and neither command actually enforces the core→Pi boundary

accepted_risks.issue: Shebang embeds `process.execPath` unquoted; a Bun path containing a space, or longer than the kernel shebang limit, makes the fake `gh` fail to exec.
Monkey-patching of Bun.spawn/spawnSync restores correctly only in LIFO order, and PATH is restored to a snapshot.
Temp dir leaks if `git init` or `git config` throws, and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`/`GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR` from the host env are not scrubbed.

Unknown-field and missing-field tests only change the number of fields. A rename that keeps the same count, with one declared field swapped for an undeclared one, is never tested. 'Exactly the declared field names' is therefore not enforced.
The counts-only test for stack.state.snapshot only tries string values. Numbers that are not valid counts are not rejected.

Values are written into `key=value` with no escaping. A string field holding whitespace or a newline (stack.guard.rejected path, stack.commit.created ref) gives a log line that is ambiguous or forged. No test pins single-line output.

AC-29 is architectural: events must go through the shared logging.ts. The console.error spy checks the format, but a deliberately bad emitter could write `[accord:stack:<level>]` directly and copy the getLogLevel() threshold.
Values are interpolated raw, so a value containing whitespace, '=' or a newline makes the `key=value` line ambiguous or lets it split across lines.

`event` is a plain `string` and the field map is untyped, so a typo or wrong field at a call site is caught only at runtime. The emitter then throws, which could abort the commit or guard path it instruments.
Value validation is partial. task, est_lines and act_lines are unchecked, negative or fractional counts pass, and a runtime `undefined` value passes the presence check.
StackEventLevel duplicates LogLevel minus 'silent'.
The docs describe telemetry/ as 'Usage accounting', which is now stale.
The trigger and sha wiring is checked by substring presence only. Statuses can be posted to the merge sha, and either trigger can lack the main branch filter.

accepted_risks.issue: The 'valid done packet' wiring row only checks that the output lacks 'Return packet validation failed'. That check also passes if the packet is never extracted (the no-packet path), so the row does not prove the validated branch ran.
trustedContractLock is called with the raw cwd, but the rest of the function uses the git toplevel, so a non-root cwd silently disables the whole check.
A restore of locked files is invisible to the orchestrator and, at the default log level, to the user. A failed restore is swallowed and emits no rejection event.
Restoring plan.json from the lock commit overwrites the whole file, including guidance[] entries added after PR0.
Provenance by commit trailer conflicts with 'the lock file is the durable record and survives squash'.
The locked-path list duplicates lockedPaths() in contract/lock.ts, and the lock path string is repeated again.
The Commit guard rule list omits the new `locked-path` rule and the existing `amend-scope` rule. Neither the `locked-file-written` restore nor the new rules appear in okf/log.md.
Stuck, and cancel after needs_input, never test what happens to locked files already edited during the amend, e.g. spec.json amended by phase-spec before phase-plan gets stuck in --replan.

resolution.note: The spec and the task steps say only that stuck clears the marker and snapshot; restore-on-stuck is not specified. A test would invent behaviour. If this matters, the engineer should decide it as a spec question, not phase-test.

accepted_risks.issue: The tampered-working-copy test checks only that no snapshot exists when openAmend refuses. It does not check that the amend is still closed, so a refusal can leave the marker and session in place and the lock guard then allows writes to locked files.
No test runs a second amend after one completes. The done path can leave the session file behind, and openAmend can snapshot from the contract tag instead of the trusted lock, and both still pass.

Today's no-reason form `/dev amend-spec <ID>` is not tested when there is no lock or no stack. Every AC-26 test passes 'some reason', so an impl that refuses a blank reason before it checks for the lock or stack breaks backward compatibility.
amendments[0].diff is checked only for the new wording, so storing the full new spec.json (not a diff) passes.
affectedAcsFromSpecDiff is not tested for changes to AC fields other than requirement, type, criterion and scenario, such as `enforcement` or `feature`.
`applyContractAmend` and the steps after it are not guarded. A throw rejects the whole `processSubagentToolResult` batch.
`stuck` and `--cancel` delete the snapshot but leave the amended spec.json and plan.json in the working tree. A follow-up `/dev amend-spec` is then refused.
The amend commit emits no `stack.commit.created`, unlike every other orchestrator commit.
The handoff note says `blocked stale tasks: …` but lists every stale id from `applyContractAmend`.
Affected ACs come only from `acceptance_criteria` entries by id, so other spec changes get an empty diff and no stale tasks.
`blockStaleTasks` re-implements the block mutation from queries/block-task.ts `blockOne`.
`setCoarsePhase` does an unlocked read-modify-write of the work item file with an untyped cast.
`AMEND_AGENTS` and the lock path are duplicated.
`parseAmendArgs` hand-rolls a whitespace split. Quotes stay in the reason, `--replan` and `--cancel` are stripped from any position, and spaces collapse.

AC-31 is claimed in ac_covered but has no runtime test, which is acceptable for an architectural AC. validate:okf checks structure but does not check that an amend-spec entry was appended. okf/references/dev-command.md:40 still documents `/dev amend-spec <ID>` without the reason, --replan and --cancel arguments.

resolution.note: AC-31 is architectural. Enforcement belongs to phase-verify-task: bun run validate:okf, validate:ste and check:biome, plus a grep for the amend-spec entry in okf/log.md.
